newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU urged to give priority to satellite communications.
newsitem.headline: EU urged to give priority to satellite communications.

text.p: The European Union must give more attention to developing a strategy for promoting and regulating satellite communications, EU Research Commissioner Edith Cresson said on Thursday.

"In contrast to the situation in the United States, where the administration has thrown all its weight behind helping its industry in the regulatory and technical sphere, in Europe this question has not yet been placed high enough on the political agenda," she said.
The French commissioner made the remarks to a conference on satellite communications in Paris that was attended by EU ministers and industry leaders. The text was distributed in Brussels.
Cresson said European politicians and the general public were underestimating the vast potential for multimedia communications by broadband satellite.
She said she and EU Industry Commissioner Martin Bangemann had organised the conference to launch a "political signal" and to ask participants to consider several key questions.
She asked the ministers and industry officials to consider how to better coordinate the EU's position on frequency allocations in the "Ka-band" used for advanced broadband communications systems.
She also asked them to consider whether to bolster research into software, equipment and components that are used in both satellite telecommunications and satellite navigation systems, she said.
"Should we organise a joint conference with the European Space Agency and the (EU) to divide the tasks?," she asked.
"Should we give priority to research with a strong commercial potential, or, taking account of budgetary restraints, should we reserve (EU) money for pure research?" she said.
